description: REGRESSION WALL for saga #811 (issue #815), guarding the terminal rule at its SECOND site — `evaluateCall`'s, reached when an unresolvable name stands in argument position. Its sibling `terminal-rule-comprehension-body` guards the comprehension-body site; this one exists because silencing `packages/runtime/src/evaluate.ts`'s terminal (returning a value instead of raising) left the whole conformance corpus green at 1002/1002 while only JavaScript unit tests noticed — measured, and the gap a domain-QA review found in this slice's own first round. `spec/execution-model.md:717-720` requires evaluation to end in "a value, a completed effect, or a diagnostic" and says skipping the construct "is not one of them, at any depth, in any argument position" — this fixture is that last clause. `executeOptions.runUnchecked` is load-bearing rather than decorative: without it the check before execution refuses the program first (`spec/execution-model.md:661-664`) and the runtime terminal is never reached, so a fixture written without it would assert the gate and quietly assert nothing about the site it is named for. The opt-out still delivers the diagnostic (`spec/execution-model.md:687-694`), which is why one is expected here. The trailing `print "after"` is the load-bearing part of the EVENTS assertion: it never runs, so the stream holds a single `instruction`. With the terminal silenced the first `print` emits its own event and the sentinel emits two more — measured as [instruction, print, instruction, print] — so this fixture reddens on exactly the mutation the diagnostics alone cannot see, because the surviving `ol-unknown-command` is the CHECKER's copy either way and is identical in both worlds.
